disposition_groups.reason: The draft treats the Union representative as mandatory in the qualifying open-source branch. Article 54(6) exempts providers of non-systemic GPAI models released under a free and open-source licence permitting access, use, modification and distribution, with public parameters including weights, architecture information and usage information. Article 53(2) separately exempts the two documentation duties under equivalent conditions. The copyright policy, public training-content summary and cooperation as necessary remain applicable. The incorrect instruction flows from the summary into the launch checklist.

disposition_groups.reason: Keep 2 August 2026 as the application date for Article 101. The Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026, the third day after its Official Journal publication on 24 July. The Omnibus added Article 113(d) for Articles 102–110 and left Article 113(b) and the general application date intact. Article 101 remains subject to the general date under Article 113. This disposition adjudicates the requested date change.

critical_checks.evidence: The bibliography gives Commission links for the Code and Taskforce, while its statutory and Omnibus citations rely on third-party sites. The required EU1 and EU2 originals are present at the paths in data/source_registry.csv. The 27 July Omnibus date, 2 August Article 101 date and 2027 legacy-model deadline are supported. The draft places the Article 101 exception next to Chapter V without identifying that Article 101 is in Chapter XII. It also presents the general date as applying to all remaining provisions, despite the staggered exceptions. Article 101(1) sets the ceiling at the higher of EUR 15 million and 3% of the preceding financial year's total worldwide turnover for specified intentional or negligent conduct. The draft omits the higher-of rule and reference year. See sources/text/aiact-consolidated.txt:2691–2775,2953–2975,3072–3076,3126–3146 and sources/text/omnibus.txt:1042–1071,1202–1206. [EUR-Lex AI Act consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/2026-07-27/eng). [Official Journal, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/ENG/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ%3AL_202601744).

The draft identifies the three model branches and states the legacy deadline, but the shared quarterly checklist gives qualifying open-source providers unnecessary work and puts applicable new-model duties after a possible 2026 launch. It omits the Article 52 notification deadline and the separate designation route. It also leaves readers without a reliable trigger for first Union placement or for identifying when the same company is a system provider as well as a model provider. See sources/text/aiact-consolidated.txt:445–454,503–522,656–667,1690–1784,3072–3076 and sources/text/commission-guidelines.txt:76–117,140–143.

The Chapter III Sections 1–3 dates for systems classified under Article 6(2)/Annex III and Article 6(1)/Annex I are 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028, respectively, subject to the Article 6(5) exception. The Annex I category can include a system that is itself a regulated product. The December 2026 date for the new Article 5 prohibitions is supported, with their system-specific conditions and exceptions. Article 50(2) applies generally from 2 August 2026 for covered systems. Article 111(4) gives only covered systems placed on the market before that date until 2 December 2026. The draft erases this condition in §§ III and VI. The June legislative approvals, 8 July signing and 24 July publication are supported. The claim that this was the second postponement is unsubstantiated in the cited evidence. The Omnibus also amended the Article 56(6) Code assessment procedure while leaving the GPAI provider compliance dates intact. See sources/text/aiact-consolidated.txt:704–753,779–796,1667–1684,1809–1814,3063–3076,3126–3146 and sources/text/omnibus.txt:443–451,749–756,1042–1071,1202–1218. [Commission Article 50 FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/transparency-obligations-under-article-50-ai-act). [European Parliament legislative procedure](https://oeil.europarl.europa.eu/oeil/en/procedure-file?reference=2025/0359(COD)).

The cumulative training threshold is greater than 10^25 FLOP and creates a presumption of high-impact capabilities. The draft correctly lists the four Article 55 duties in broad terms. It omits the Article 51(1)(b) designation route, which can capture a model below the compute threshold, and Article 52(1)'s requirement to notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks of meeting, or learning the model will meet, the relevant criterion. Exceptional rebuttal grounds are submitted with that notice. Path C also presents the Code's Safety and Security chapter as an added obligation, although Article 55(2) permits alternative adequate evidence and gives a presumption only for obligations covered by harmonised standards. See sources/text/aiact-consolidated.txt:1690–1716,1771–1786,3578–3594 and sources/text/commission-guidelines.txt:89–117. The superscript is preserved at sources/raw/aiact-consolidated.html:9627.
